references.text: The preceding verse in the same passage, where Jesus exhorts the disciples to have their belts fastened and their lamps burning – a readiness that leads directly into the parable of waiting for the master ([ref:Luk 12:35|Luke 12:35]).

Jesus continues by praising those who are awake when the Lord comes, saying he himself will serve them – a direct extension of the image of waiting and opening the door immediately ([ref:Luk 12:37-38|Luke 12:37–38]).
Jesus summarizes the parable: "Be ready, for the Son of Man comes at an hour you do not expect." This underscores the same point about vigilance ([ref:Luk 12:40|Luke 12:40]).

Jesus' teaching in Mark about keeping watch, where the master goes away and puts his servants in charge, exhorting them to be awake because they do not know when the master will come – a very close parallel passage ([ref:Mark 13:33-37|Mark 13:33–37]).
The parable of the ten virgins waiting for the bridegroom – the same theme of wedding, waiting, and readiness, and opening the door when the bridegroom arrives ([ref:Matt 25:1-13|Matthew 25:1–13]).
Jesus' exhortation to keep watch because you do not know when the Lord will come, parallel with Luke 12:35–40 ([ref:Matt 24:42-44|Matthew 24:42–44]).

Jesus says: "I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him." The motif of knocking on the door and opening immediately is shared with Luke 12:36 ([ref:Åp 3:20|Revelation 3:20]).
James exhorts believers to wait patiently for the Lord's coming and says that the Lord stands at the door – the same expectation of the Lord's imminent return ([ref:Jak 5:7-9|James 5:7–9]).
Paul writes that "we await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ" – the same expectant attitude toward the Lord's coming ([ref:Fil 3:20|Philippians 3:20]).

We are to live "soberly, righteously, and godly ... while we wait for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" – readiness and expectation as central themes ([ref:Tit 2:12-13|Titus 2:12–13]).

Peter exhorts believers to gird up their minds, be sober, and set their hope fully on the grace that will be brought to them when Jesus Christ is revealed – similar exhortations about readiness ([ref:1 Pet 1:13|1 Peter 1:13]).
